To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) O3 exposure or O3 uptake reduced net assimilation and gross photosynthesis of ponderosa pine; 2) the reduction of gas exchange was greatest at the most polluted site; 3) O3 exposure and O3 uptake were equally effective in reducing gas exchange, and 4) drought stress synergistically reduced gas exchange in the moderately polluted site.
O3 exposure or O3 uptake reduces photosynthetic carbon acquisition of ponderosapine trees, and that this effect is enhanced by drought stress.

1) the effects of O3 on photosynthesis of ponderosa pine are best described as a linear response to O3 exposure or O3 uptake, and 2) the effects of late summer drought and O3 on photosynthetic rates are synergistic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ozone (O3) on the carbon balance of trees.
the effects of ozone on ponderosa pine, a tree species that is common throughout western North America and that is an important component of the forests of the Sierra Nevada and the Cascade Range.
the effect of pollutant exposure on the physiology of trees, and how that effect is modified by environmental conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
O3 uptake and drought synergistically affect carbon uptake in 40- yr-old ponderosa pine.
O3 exposure, uptake and drought stress reduce photosynthetic carbon acquisition in 40- yr-old ponderosa pines, but the effect of drought stress is only evident at a moderate O3 exposure site.
O3 exposure or O3 uptake reduced A and Pg in ponderosa pine in the field, and drought stress reduced A and Pg, and synergistically reduced Pg in the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cumulative O3 exposure/uptake of 20–25 mol m−2 is deleterious to ponderosa pine photosynthesis.
cumulative O3 exposure and uptake reduced carbon acquisition of ponderosas in all years and sites.
O3 exposure or O3 uptake reduced carbon assimilation, with the effect being slightly more pronounced on gross photosynthesis than on net assimilation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O3 uptake and exposure can be used to assess O3 effects on carbon acquisition in ponderosa pine, and that the effect of drought stress on carbon acquisition can be statistically assessed.
O3 exposure or cumulative uptake is a better predictor of gas exchange response than O3 exposure alone.
O3 exposure or O3 uptake can be used to predict the effects of O3 on gas exchange in natural stands of ponderosa pine, and that the combined effects of O3 and drought can be predicted.
